newsitem.title: UK: Hilfiger, Littlewoods in trademark dispute.
newsitem.headline: Hilfiger, Littlewoods in trademark dispute.

text.p: Fashion sportswear company Tommy Hilfiger Corp. has accused Littlewoods, Britain's largest private retail group, of infringing on its trademarks, Hilfiger said Friday.

Hilfiger, which plans to open its first London store later this year, said it launched the legal action after Littlewoods Warehouses Ltd refused to provide information about the sale of counterfeit Tommy Hilfiger clothing.
"The company alleges that Littlewoods has been selling merchandise that infringes various Tommy Hilfiger trademarks," and is seeking compensation and damages, Hilfiger said in a statement.
In a brief statement, Littlewoods responded that it would not knowingly sell any counterfeit merchandise and was investigating Hilfiger's complaint.

"Littlewoods Home Shopping Group maintains a policy of selling branded products that to the best of our knowledge are original products. Littlewoods would not knowingly sell any counterfeit merchandise," the company said.
Hilfiger designs, sources and markets men's and boys' sportswear under the Tommy Hilfiger trademark. The company said it planned to open one London store this fall and another next year.
